identity.title: Transcutaneous electric acupoint stimulation alleviates remifentanil-induced hyperalgesia in patients undergoing thyroidectomy: a randomized controlled trial
identity.notes: Yanqing Chen,Yusheng Yao,Yihuan Wu,Dongsheng Dai,Qiuyan Zhao,Liangcheng Qiu; IJCEM8(4):5781–5787,IJCEM0006509; publishedApril30,2015.

source_review.full_publication: Read all seven PDF pages, including references.

design.population: 60 female adults18–60,ASA I–II,elective thyroidectomy under GA; Fujian Provincial Hospital August–December2014.
design.intervention: BilateralLI4/PC6,2/10Hz,6–9mA for30min before anesthesia; intensity to muscle twitch and DeQi.
design.randomization: Computer-generated list,1:1; sealed envelopes, but opacity/sequential numbering not stated.
design.blinding: Patients,investigator,anesthetist,surgeons,recovery nurses and statistical analyst claimed blinded; awake perceptible stimulation versus inactive sham can reveal allocation; operator necessarily knows.
design.attrition: One TEAS participant discontinued for unspecified protocol breach;59/60 analyzed.

regimen.pca: Demand-only sufentanil0.05µg/kg per bolus if VNRS≥4;10-min lockout; continuous infusion not allowed. No mass concentration or absolute consumed dose reported.
regimen.rescue: PCA delivered sufentanil rescue; additional systemic opioid use is insufficiently reported.
regimen.anesthesia: Propofol2mg/kg and remifentanil target5ng/mL induction; remifentanil5ng/mL plus sevoflurane maintenance to BIS40–60.

independent_outcomes.finding: Peri-incisional between-group reductionP<.001;forearmP=.328. No numerical point labels; do not extract estimated graph values. Threshold depends on patient reporting first pain, not purely objective.
independent_outcomes.qualification: Table1 baselineforearm control93.9 contrasts visually with Figure3A baselinecontrol near98; do not infer exact graph point. No remifentanil-free arm, so remifentanil-specific causation is not isolated.

independent_outcomes.window: Within24h; precise time origin not stated
independent_outcomes.qualification: Results show LONGER time withTEAS;discussion incorrectly says reduces time.
0.05µg/kg per delivered bolus. Counts are notabsolute mass; no conversion through mean weight.
Not postoperative. PrintedP=.461 inconsistent with conventional independentt using mean/SD/n(tabout2.59). Do not repair.

source_conflicts: Table1 intraoperative remifentanil mean/SD/n does not reconcile withP=.461
Forearm baseline graph position conflicts with Table1; postoperativegraphvalues remainunextracted
Discussion says time-to-rescue reduced whereas Table2 and results show longer
independence: Independent ofS062 supported by disjointAug–Dec2014 versusJan–May2015 enrollment, different ethicsIDs,60vs84 randomized and remifentanil/sufentanil versus induction-sufentanil/morphine analgesic protocols. Same center and TEAS settings are not evidence of duplication.

opioid_candidate.reason: 24h rescue-administration median/IQR is extractable as an opioid-demand count endpoint, but not absolute mass or a primary mean/SD systemic opioid endpoint. Weight-dependent sufentanil boluses prevent group-mean-weight conversion.

1.2: Sealed envelopes reported without opacity, sequential numbering or safeguard details.
1.3: Demographic means broadly similar;one missing ASA category and inconsistentP reporting do not demonstrate a failed allocation sequence.
2.1: Awake6–9mA DeQi and muscle twitch versus inactive sham likely perceptible, despite blinding claim.
2.2: Stimulation operator must distinguish active delivery from sham.
2.3: One unspecified protocol breach; whether trial-context-induced is unknown.
2.4: No detail of protocol breach or effects on rescue behavior.
2.5: OneTEAS breach; insufficient detail to judge comparable departures in arms.
2.6: One randomizedTEAS participant excluded for protocol breach.
2.7: One of60 omitted; unlikely substantial effect on median3vs7 rescue counts or5vs13PONV events.
4.1: Delivered rescue-administration count is appropriate for opioid demand, not for unreported absolute opioid mass.
4.2: Standardized demand-only PCA and same follow-up24h.
4.3: Outcome-collecting investigator/recovery nurses were blinded; electronically delivered PCA counts are objective records.
4.4: Objective delivered count; participant-influenced self-dosing is not differential outcome measurement.
4.5: Objective delivered count; no evidence of differential recording.
5.1: No trial registration identifier or dated analysis plan reported.
5.2: Secondary rescue-count endpoint reported but no prospective detailed protocol verifies definition and24h clock.
5.3: No dated SAP; selection of summaries/analyses before unblinding cannot be established.

rob_independent.reason: Sealed-envelope safeguards incompletely specified,one unspecified protocol-breach exclusion and no prospective plan. Near-complete follow-up and standardized objective delivery counts support lowD3/D4; subjective pain/PONV require separateD4 judgments.
